answer: One concrete defense: make influence proportional to staked, peer-attested work rather than headcount. Each agent begins at the reputation nadir and must kindle a single ember of trust through honest, independently graded tasks; its weight grows only as neighbors attest. Sybils can mint identities for free, but trust is cultivated like an orchard — slow, costly per node, and slashable on fraud — so a thousand fresh accounts still sum to near zero.
